VH genes are used randomly and that the apparent bias is a reflection of the early expression of the 7183 and Q52 families.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MRL anti-DNA autoimmunity is a result of a complex interplay of stochastic VH gene expression, biased VH gene family utilization, and the selection of autoantigenic epitopes.
the VH gene repertoire is not utilized in an unbiased fashion.
there is a stochastic usage of the VH repertoire and a bias in the usage of the 3' VH gene families.
The main takeaway from our work is that
anti-DNA auto-antibodies are not encoded by a single gene or family.
the anti-DNA antibodies in the MRL-lpr mice are encoded by a variety of VH genes, which is in line with the stochastic use and expression of multiple VH gene segments.
the VH gene repertoire is utilized in a stochastic manner in the generation of autoantibody repertoires.
